title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: anomia / blessed–miserable chain; unspoken minor we are not blessed
pass_a_gloss: You say the Psalmist's names for sins can signify that first rebellion of Adam no less than Cain's murder or Israel's rebellion. You add it is anomia, the Apostle's word citing this place: granted; what follows Placeus does not yet see—the same can be said of Cain, Sodom, Absalom, or any crime. But you yourself conclude: according to the Apostle using the Prophet, blessed is he to whom sins are not imputed, miserable he to whom they are; and since our whole misery is from Adam's first sin, if that is imputed we are miserable, if not we are blessed. You left us, Placeus thinks, the unspoken minor: But we are not blessed; therefore that sin is imputed to us.
pass_b_english: You say the names by which the Psalmist called sins can signify that first rebellion of Adam, namely no less than Cain's murder, or the Israelite people's rebellion. You add that it is anomia, which word the Apostle used in citing this place: Be it so; what follows from that I do not yet understand: for the same may be said of Cain's murder, of the crime of Sodom, of Absalom's incest and rebellion, and finally of any other crime of anyone. But you yourself conclude something; let us hear you then. From there, you say, we ought to conclude according to the Apostle using the Prophet's words, that he is blessed to whom sins are not imputed, and consequently that he is miserable to whom sins are imputed, and since our whole misery is from Adam's first sin, if that sin is imputed to us, we are miserable, if on the contrary it is not imputed to us, we are blessed. You left us, I think, the minor to be subsumed: But we are not blessed: Therefore that sin is imputed to us.
source_text: Ais nomina, quibus Psaltes peccata nuncupavit, posse primam illam Adami rebellionem significare, nempe, haud minus, quam, vel Caini homicidium, vel populi Israelitici rebellionem. Adjicis eam esse ἀνομίαν, qua voce usus est Apostolus in citando hoc loco: Esto; quid inde sequatur nondum intelligo: idem enim de Caini homicidio, de Sodomorum crimine, de Absalomi incestum & rebellione, & denique de quovis alio cujusvis scelere dicere licet. Sed tu ipse aliquid concludis, te igitur audiamus. Inde, inquis, concludere debemus secundum Apostolum verbis Prophetae utentem, illum esse beatum cui peccata non imputantur, & ex consequenti, illum esse miserum cui peccata imputantur, & cum miseria nostra tota sit a peccato primo Adami, si peccatum illud nobis imputatur, nos esse miseros, si e contra nobis non imputetur, nos esse beatos. Tu nobis, opinor, subsumendum reliquisti, Atqui non sumus beati: Ergo nobis peccatum illud imputatur.
